cases.prompt: We are launching a support chatbot that can issue refunds through a tool call. What should our test plan cover before launch?

any.why: covers tool calls or their effects

expectations: Covers grounding or hallucination against the real source of truth (refund policy, order data).
Covers tool calls: the right tool, correct arguments, and the resulting side effect or end state of the refund.
Covers prompt injection or adversarial users and multi-turn conversations.
Recommends running each scenario several times and reporting a pass rate rather than a single pass or fail.

cases.prompt: This test for our agent fails randomly. How should I rewrite the assertion?

any.regex: pass rate|several times|multiple runs|repeat|runs? (it|each) \d|5 times|N times
any.why: treats the test as repeated runs with a pass rate

expectations: Explains that an exact string match is wrong for non-deterministic output.
Replaces it with property assertions, such as checking that the reply contains the correct fact (5 to 7 business days) or matches required content.
Mentions an LLM judge with a written rubric only for qualities code cannot check, or says code checks come first.
Suggests running the case several times and judging by pass rate.
